summary.text: Jeff Foster is the Democratic candidate for Wisconsin State Senate District 23 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Republican Romaine Quinn.
A retired dairy farmer and social worker from Dunn County, he ran for Wisconsin State Assembly District 67 in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Jeff Foster was born in Wisconsin, graduated from Hamilton High School, and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 1979 and a graduate degree from the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh in 1988.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he worked in child protective services as a social worker on the Menominee Reservation before buying a farm in Dunn County, where he became the sixth person in Wisconsin to milk sheep commercially.
He said he co-founded the Wisconsin Sheep Dairy Cooperative and served as its first president, and later worked for and retired from Xcel Energy.
Foster was the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin State Assembly District 67 in 2024 and lost the general election to incumbent David Armstrong.

He said in the survey that he ran for Dunn County Supervisor in 2026 and has been a delegate to the Wisconsin 3rd Congressional District Democratic Convention and the Wisconsin State Democratic Convention.
He defeated Richard Pulcher in the Democratic primary for Wisconsin State Senate District 23 on August 11, 2026.

Foster listed freedom, family and community as the themes of his campaign in the survey, citing reproductive freedom, voting access, protection from gun violence, high-quality child care and public education, paid medical leave, and affordable health care.
He has been affiliated with the Wisconsin Farmers Union.
